item.text:
**Bottom Line**  
Mixed. Marcos did put real policy attention on several vulnerable groups in 2024: children, PWDs, senior citizens, poor households, disaster-hit communities, women survivors of abuse, and farmers. But the record also shows strong negative evidence on Indigenous peoples, labor organizers, women’s groups, journalists, and other marginalized voices through red-tagging and coercive politics. So the answer is “yes in some service-delivery areas, no as a clean general pattern.”

**Accepted Claims**
- **PBBM orders 4Ps expansion to cover pregnant, lactating women to ensure children’s health, well-being in first 1000 days** — Presidential Communications Office, Jun. 11, 2024: [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-4ps-expansion-to-cover-pregnant-lactating-women-to-ensure-childrens-health-well-being-in-first-1000-days/)  
  Marcos expanded the 4Ps to pregnant and lactating women and framed the move as improving children’s early-life health and nutrition. This is direct prioritization of children and mothers. `6B.3`; also `6B.2`, `6B.1`.

- **PBBM fosters PWD-friendly Philippines** — Presidential Communications Office, Jul. 23, 2024: [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-fosters-pwd-friendly-philippines/)  
  The administration said it was pushing special interventions and incentives for persons with disabilities, and Marcos said PhilHealth would launch benefits for PWD children and senior citizens. This is strong evidence for prioritizing disabled people and the elderly. `6B.3`; also `6B.2`, `6B.1`.

- **PBBM okays one-stop system for reporting child rights’ violations** — Presidential Communications Office, Dec. 10, 2024: [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-okays-one-stop-system-for-reporting-child-rights-violations/)  
  Marcos approved the MAKABATA program and helpline for children in need of special protection, including abused, neglected, exploited, trafficked, disabled, and HIV-affected children. This is direct, targeted prioritization of vulnerable children. `6B.3`; also `6B.2`, `6B.1`.

- **PBBM calls for comprehensive national flood-control plan to protect communities, production areas** — Presidential Communications Office, Jul. 26, 2024: [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-calls-for-comprehensive-national-flood-control-plan-to-protect-communities-production-areas/)  
  After Typhoon Carina and Habagat, Marcos framed flood control as protection for communities and production areas. This favors poor and disaster-exposed communities, which are often the most vulnerable. `6B.3`; also `6B.2`, `5B.6`, `5B.9`.

- **SWS survey: PBBM very good on helping disaster victims, improving children’s quality of education, helping the poor** — Presidential Communications Office, Sep. 14, 2024: [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/sws-survey-pbbm-very-good-on-helping-disaster-victims-improving-childrens-quality-of-education-helping-the-poor/)  
  The administration highlighted survey evidence that it was performing strongly on disaster response, education, and aid to the poor. This is broad positive evidence for prioritizing vulnerable groups, especially children and poor households. `6B.3`; also `6B.2`, `6B.1`, `5B.8`.

- **PBBM signs law to further boost PH rice industry** — Presidential Communications Office, Dec. 9, 2024: [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-inks-law-to-further-boost-ph-rice-industry/)  
  Extending RCEF is a structural farm-support move aimed at productivity and food security, which matters disproportionately for rural poor households. This is pro-poor-region and food-security prioritization. `6B.3`; also `6B.2`, `5B.10`, `5B.8`.

- **President Marcos unveils DA’s Agri-Puhunan Program targeting 1.2 million hectares with low-cost credit and market support** — Department of Agriculture, Sep. 13, 2024: [link](https://www.da.gov.ph/president-marcos-unveils-das-agri-puhunan-program-targeting-1-2-million-hectares-with-low-cost-credit-and-market-support/)  
  The program gave farmers low-cost credit, subsistence support, and market access. That is direct support for poor rural communities and small farmers. `6B.3`; also `6B.2`, `5B.8`.

- **PBBM orders implementation of amnesty program to communist rebels** — Presidential Communications Office, Apr. 4, 2024: [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-implementation-of-amnesty-program-to-communist-rebels/)  
  The amnesty move can be read as reintegration and de-escalation toward politically marginalized or unpopular actors. It is weaker than the service-delivery items above, but it does show some inclusion of conflict-affected groups. `6B.3`; also `5B.8`, `6B.1`.

- **PBBM sees peaceful, orderly BARMM poll** — Presidential Communications Office, Jun. 24, 2024: [link](https://mirror.pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-sees-peaceful-orderly-barmm-poll/)  
  Marcos publicly urged a peaceful, transparent first BARMM parliamentary election. This supports a limited prioritization of a historically marginalized region, though it is still mostly rhetoric and election management. `6B.3`; also `5B.8`, `6B.1`.

- **PBBMS SONA highlights significant progress in BARMM, Bangsamoro leaders react** — Presidential Communications Office, Jul. 24, 2024: [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbms-sona-highlights-significant-progress-in-barmm-bangsamoro-leaders-react/)  
  The administration emphasized Marawi rehabilitation and peace-agreement implementation, which indicates regional attention to a historically marginalized conflict zone. This is positive, but narrower than full equality of treatment. `6B.3`; also `6B.1`, `5B.8`.

- **Human Rights Watch: Philippines: Dangerous ‘Red Tagging’ of Labor Leaders** — Human Rights Watch, Sep. 25, 2024: [link](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders)  
  HRW says officials and security actors threatened union leaders and also targeted women’s groups, Indigenous peoples, journalists, teachers, and judges. This is strong evidence against consistent prioritization of vulnerable communities. `6B.3`; also `6B.1`, `5B.8`, `6B.8`.

- **Human Rights Watch: Philippines: “Red-Tagging” Puts Activists at Risk** — Human Rights Watch, Jan. 11, 2024: [link](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/philippines-red-tagging-puts-activists-risk)  
  HRW said red-tagging under Marcos put leftist activists and critics at serious risk and constricted democratic space. This undercuts a claim that marginalized political groups were being prioritized or protected. `6B.3`; also `6B.1`, `5B.8`, `6B.8`.

- **Freedom House: Philippines Freedom in the World 2024** — Freedom House, 2024: [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024)  
  Freedom House said Indigenous people faced harassment and violence in Mindanao, LGBT+ people lacked full protection, and disability protections were weakly enforced. It also noted women’s political representation remained concentrated in political families. This is broad negative background evidence on marginalized-group prioritization. `6B.3`; also `5B.8`, `6B.1`.

- **Amnesty says no progress in sight for Marcos Admin on human rights issues** — Amnesty Philippines, May 8, 2024: [link](https://www.amnesty.org.ph/2024/05/amnesty-says-no-progress-in-sight-for-marcos-admin-on-human-rights-issues/)  
  Amnesty said Indigenous peoples, student activists, journalists, lawyers, and other vulnerable groups faced red-tagging, threats, and harassment under a climate of impunity. This is strong evidence against broad prioritization of marginalized communities. `6B.3`; also `6B.1`, `5B.8`, `6B.8`.

- **Philippines: “I turned my fear into courage”: Red-tagging and state violence against young human rights defenders in the Philippines** — Amnesty International, Oct. 14, 2024: [link](https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa35/8574/2024/en/)  
  Amnesty said Marcos-era actors weaponized misinformation and anti-terror framing against activists, teachers, journalists, and others, creating fear. This is direct counterevidence to a clean vulnerable-groups priority finding. `6B.3`; also `6B.1`, `5B.8`, `6B.8`.

**Search Gap**
- I found good evidence on children, PWDs, women survivors, poor households, farmers, and BARMM.
- I found much less direct evidence on elderly people beyond PWD/senior-citizen references in official releases, and almost nothing specific on housing access for marginalized groups in 2024.
- Net: Marcos clearly prioritized some vulnerable groups in targeted programs, but the negative rights environment means this was selective rather than a clean across-the-board commitment.
